sections.title: 1. Credentials and the data red line
sections.summary: Highest priority, non-negotiable: credentials never enter the repository or any conversation artifact; the committed surface (game settings / playbook / experience-growth Mod / evolution output) is equally off limits for sensitive values, and every example uses synthetic data.

rules.text: Never write a credential, key or token into the repository — including code, documentation, commit messages and Mod example data.
Never write a credential into any conversation artifact: reports, summaries, issue/PR descriptions, pasted log excerpts.

No sensitive information may enter a committed resource — the committed surface explicitly includes: game settings `data/config.json`, this playbook `data/playbook.json`, the experience/growth (evolution) Mod and its output, and every other Mod resource or document committed with the repository.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition, not in the original AGENTS.md)

rules.text: The runtime KV family `settings.*` is no exception for sensitive values: the static defaults (`data/config.json`) and the dynamic overrides (`settings.*` written by `config.set`) only ever hold non-sensitive behavior switches, numbers and experience text (such as `evolution.mode` / `gates.require_all_green` / `evolution.max_per_run`).

Sensitive values — LLM API keys, tokens, database/object-storage connection strings, subagent model parameters (`YGG_SUBAGENT_*`) — live only in the local `.env` / `.env.local` (both git-ignored) and in no other file.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition); AGENTS.md §1 rule 1, §3 dispatch discipline 2

rules.text: Mod resources and reports may show key names only (such as `YGG_LLM_*`, `YGG_SUBAGENT_MODEL`), never values — including narrative text, `beats`/`prompts`, the closing review and any walk report.

End-of-run evolution output (suggestion text, the review artifact, and any resource edit made from it) also counts as committed surface: never write a sensitive value into a Mod or a report as "accumulated experience".
Local development credentials always go through `.env` / `.env.local` (both git-ignored, mode 600); `.env.example` carries key names only, never values.
Reports, documentation, commit messages and Mod example data show key names only, never values.
Examples and test data are always synthetic; never introduce real personal data.
After a violation, list honestly what was exposed (the specific file plus the content location), without downplaying or arguing; then stop the affected operations and wait for the user.

sections.title: 2. Repository shape
sections.summary: A Rust five-crate workspace plus pnpm packages, a Godot client and the in-repo .ygg harness; three shape invariants: a single source for decisions, a single source for schemas, and a zero-dependency core.

rules.text: The decision table in `docs/CONTEXT.md` is the single source of truth for project decisions; any new decision produced by a design discussion (D11+) must be written back into that table.
An implementation that conflicts with the decision table is a defect: never let a decision drift silently on the grounds that "the implementation is already done".
Resource format contracts live only in `packages/schema/schemas/` (D15): the TS side (ajv) and the Rust side (jsonschema crate) read the same file, and neither side may keep an inline copy.
A schema constrains the resource file format, not Mod logic — the executable interface of a Mod is a Lua script (D11).
`crates/ygg-core` has a zero-dependency invariant: no internal module, no DOM/platform API, no rendering library; the allowlist is serde / serde_json / thiserror only.
VM dependencies such as mlua may appear only in `crates/ygg-sandbox` (D12).

Dependency direction is one-way: `ygg-sandbox` → `ygg-core` + `ygg-schema`; `ygg-wasm` → `ygg-sandbox`; `ygg-lint` has no ygg-* kernel dependency; `ygg-schema` and `ygg-core` have no code dependency edge.
rules.basis: docs/CONTEXT.md §4 (inter-module dependency constraints); the Cargo.toml header note of each crate

sections.title: 3. Branch management
sections.summary: master accepts merges only; all development happens on feature branches that integrate through the standing `develop` branch (feature → develop → master); every merge is no-FF.

rules.text: Never develop directly on master; master accepts merges only.
All work (documentation included) happens on a feature branch named `feature/<topic>` or `docs/<topic>`.
Every branch merge (feature → develop → master) uses `git merge --no-ff`; fast-forward is forbidden on every hop.
Keep the merge node so an iteration batch (such as `v<date>.<n>`) stays traceable in the history graph and can be rolled back as a whole — that is the purpose of no-FF, not a style preference.

`develop` is the standing integration branch (physical branch name; `origin/develop` exists): every requirement closeout rebases its feature branch onto `develop` and merges it into `develop` with `--no-ff`; `develop` joins `master` only at a round closeout, and no feature branch ever merges into `master` — the only edge into `master` is the round-level `develop` → `master` merge.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Push a feature branch to origin once its verification passes (for collaboration and backup).
Opening a PR and merging into master are triggered explicitly by the user; the agent never starts them on its own.

sections.title: 3b. Lane worktrees
sections.summary: One worktree and one `.lane` plaque per lane; occupy means plaque up, close means plaque down, and a worktree is never shared.

rules.text: Lane worktrees use the conventional path `~/tmp/worktrees/yggdrasill-<n>` and sit detached at the `origin/master` head while idle.
Every lane worktree keeps a `.lane` file at its root (never committed): `LANE_OCCUPIED=true|false` plus `LANE_TASK` / `LANE_BRANCH` / `LANE_SINCE`.
Always read `.lane` before dispatching: `LANE_OCCUPIED=true` means pick another lane or wait for the release; a missing file counts as free but the plaque must then be created.
Occupying means plaque up; closing means plaque down — once the task is merged or abandoned, set `LANE_OCCUPIED` back to false and clear the task fields.
Two tasks may never share one worktree; before dispatching, `git status` must be clean (except `.lane`).
